newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Stable futures send Bund volatility south.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Stable futures send Bund volatility south.

text.p: A stable futures market and relaxed trade ahead of Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's Senate testimony conspired to push Bund volatility lower on Tuesday, traders said.

Greenspan presents his Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on the economy on Wednesday, although the House Banking Committee postponed the second leg of Greenspan's semiannual testimony from Thursday to March 5.
"Bund vol is off across the board," said a trader at a French bank in London. "It's not coming off really hard, just steadily eroding."

April Bund volatility on June Bund futures was offered at 5.51 percent, the same level as Monday's bid. In May options, volatility traded earlier at 5.56 percent and was being offered lower by 1245 GMT.
June options were down about 0.10 percent to 5.46/5.52 percent by the same time. June Bund futures traded on LIFFE were up 0.14 at 103.37.
Traders said there were limited strategies going through in the market this session, but in recent days it had been dominated by June combination trades.
They involved paper buying of June puts at the 101.00 strike, and selling June 104.00 calls.
"That's traded around 15,000 times, and is supposed to be part of an overall 20,000," said a trader at a British brokerage in London. "The delta is big, and it's being done versus the future."
Delta is the measure of change in the value of the option, compared with the change in the price of the underlying future.
The so-called combo is a synthetic short, and hedging it against the future takes the edge off the volatility. This trade would benefit from a large downward move in the underlying future.
"I don't think that future will go sharply down," said the British brokerage trader. "It looks as though the futures are consolidating, with a bull flag forming, and a breakout on the upside due."
